text: Sector boosts (SEMI/AI multipliers) leaked -24.8 Sharpe in backtest. Removed in May 2 sprint. DO NOT re-introduce blanket sector boosts; instead use sector_alpha tracking + per-pattern hypothesis testing.
author: sun-may-3-sprint

text: Backtester proved 5 specific tickers (UNH, TEAM, SMCI, DIS, SCHW) have negative R-multiples across 20 months. Not noise. Excluded permanently in config.yaml. Always validate edge per-ticker, not just per-strategy.
author: sun-may-3-sprint

text: New ML/statistical features ship in OBSERVE-MODE first. Never wire a new signal to auto-block or auto-flip until it has 30+ samples AND statistical significance. Pattern proven on EV-gate, applies to Pillar 1 L4 (hypothesis engine) and Pillar 2 (wisdom_consultant).
author: sun-may-3-sprint

text: Pillar 1 (Brain) MUST ship before Pillar 2 (Wisdom) which MUST ship before Pillar 4 (Auto-Adapt). Otherwise wisdom has no inputs and auto-adapt has no signals to flip on. Don't reorder.
author: sun-may-3-sprint

text: Never average down a losing position.
author: Edwin Lefèvre / Jesse Livermore

text: Cut losses quickly; let winners run.
author: Edwin Lefèvre / Jesse Livermore

text: The big money is in the big swing — sit tight in a winning trend.
author: Edwin Lefèvre / Jesse Livermore

text: Markets are never wrong, opinions often are.
author: Edwin Lefèvre / Jesse Livermore

text: Don't trade every day; wait for setups with clear edge.
author: Edwin Lefèvre / Jesse Livermore

text: Know what you own and why you own it.
author: Peter Lynch

text: Avoid hot tips and stocks 'everyone' is talking about.
author: Peter Lynch

text: Small caps with strong earnings growth often outperform.
author: Peter Lynch

text: It's futile to predict the economy; predict the company.
author: Peter Lynch

text: Selling winners too soon and holding losers is the cardinal sin.
author: Peter Lynch

text: Always buy with a margin of safety.
author: Benjamin Graham

text: Mr. Market is moody — exploit his swings, don't follow him.
author: Benjamin Graham

text: Investment is most intelligent when most businesslike.
author: Benjamin Graham

text: The investor's chief problem is likely to be himself.
author: Benjamin Graham

text: Distinguish investment from speculation; never confuse the two.
author: Benjamin Graham

text: Risk control is the most important attribute of a successful trader.
author: Jack Schwager

text: Develop an edge before sizing up; method before money.
author: Jack Schwager

text: Discipline is the bridge between strategy and results.
author: Jack Schwager

text: The trade you don't take can save more than the trade you do.
author: Jack Schwager

text: Lose your opinion, not your money — adapt to evidence.
author: Jack Schwager

text: Buy strong earnings (current quarter EPS up 25%+).
author: William O'Neil

text: Buy stocks making new 52-week highs from sound bases.
author: William O'Neil

text: Volume should expand on breakout — 50%+ above average.
author: William O'Neil

text: Trade with the market trend, not against it.
author: William O'Neil

text: Each trade is independent — don't let prior outcomes bias you.
author: Mark Douglas

text: A consistent process produces consistent results.
author: Mark Douglas

text: Anything can happen — accept uncertainty as the only certainty.
author: Mark Douglas

text: You don't need to know what will happen to make money.
author: Mark Douglas

text: Don't fight the tape — ride confirmed trends.
author: Michael Covel

text: Most trades will be small losers; a few will be big winners.
author: Michael Covel

text: Exit rules matter more than entry rules.
author: Michael Covel

text: Diversify across uncorrelated markets to smooth equity curve.
author: Michael Covel

text: Diversify across uncorrelated bets — the holy grail of investing.
author: Ray Dalio

text: Pain + reflection = progress; analyze every loss.
author: Ray Dalio

text: Don't confuse a good outcome with a good decision (or vice versa).
author: Ray Dalio

text: Know what kind of regime you're in (growth/inflation rising/falling).
author: Ray Dalio

text: The biggest risk is the one you don't see — stress-test for tails.
author: Ray Dalio

text: When you're sure you're right, bet big — but verify the thesis daily.
author: George Soros

text: Reflexivity: prices influence fundamentals which influence prices.
author: George Soros

text: It's not whether you're right or wrong — it's how much you make when right and lose when wrong.
author: George Soros

text: When the thesis breaks, exit immediately — don't rationalize.
author: George Soros

text: Markets reward those who recognize regime change first.
author: George Soros

text: Risk means more things can happen than will happen.
author: Howard Marks

text: Second-level thinking beats first-level thinking — always ask 'and then what?'
author: Howard Marks

text: The most dangerous words: 'It's different this time.'
author: Howard Marks

text: Buy fear, sell greed — be contrarian when sentiment is extreme.
author: Howard Marks

text: It's not what you buy, it's what you pay — entry price is everything.
author: Howard Marks
